draft.title: Health, wellbeing and illness
card: Health and wellbeing
Health and wellbeing have five dimensions: physical, social, emotional, mental and spiritual. A person's health in one dimension can affect the others.
Illness
Illness is a person's own experience of being unwell. It can be felt even when a doctor finds no disease.
Dynamic
Health, wellbeing and illness change over time, sometimes within a day. A person can move up or down in each dimension.
Subjective
They are also subjective, which means they depend on a person's own view and experience. Two people in the same situation may judge their health differently.
draft.remember: Health, wellbeing and illness change over time and depend on the person's own view.

a.q: Which statement best shows that health and wellbeing are dynamic?
opts: A student feels well on Monday but unwell by Friday
A student rates their health higher than a friend does
A student has both physical and social dimensions of health
A student feels unwell although tests show no disease
a.why: Dynamic means changing over time, and a shift from well to unwell during a week shows this. Rating health differently from a friend shows subjectivity, not change, and it is the most tempting wrong option.
a.clue: Dynamic is about change across time.

b.q: Priya has a cold and says she feels terrible. Her brother had the same cold last week and says it was barely noticeable. Which idea does this best show?
opts: Illness is subjective, as it depends on the person
Illness is dynamic, as it changes from week to week
Illness only affects the physical dimension of health
Illness is only present when a doctor confirms a disease
b.why: Two people with the same cold describe it differently, so the experience depends on the person. That is subjectivity. It is not mainly about change over time, because the two experiences happened at different times but are compared by how they felt, not how they shifted.
b.clue: Compare how two people see the same cold.

a.best: A student feels well on Monday but unwell by Friday

b.best: Illness is subjective, as it depends on the person

problems.detail: Two of the three wrong options use 'only' ('only affects the physical dimension', 'only present when a doctor confirms'). The card says one dimension 'can' affect others and illness 'can' be felt without a diagnosed disease, so these absolute words let a student rule them out without knowing the idea. That leaves a two-way choice.
